title: Independent security review submission (record.json)
description: The machine-readable contract for one review submission. VERIFY_SUBMISSION.py enforces exactly this file (it reads the required lists, enums, patterns, and x-aliases from here, so the schema and the validator cannot drift), plus four checks a JSON Schema cannot express: the alias pairs must be equal; artifact_digest and independently_computed_digest must each be one of the subject artifact's five digests in ARTIFACT_IDENTITY.json; review_start must not postdate review_end; and independence.is_release_decision_authority true requires independence.policy_exception. A record carrying fixtureClass TEST_FIXTURE_ONLY is never a submission. The five intake-alias fields exist because the submission must also pass the Phase 9 intake validation unchanged (qualification/phase9/tools/intake.py): reviewer, scope, date, disposition, artifactDigest are the spellings that boundary checks, and this contract requires them equal to their canonical counterparts.

schema.description: names the contract version this record answers

reviewer_id.description: reviewer identity or approved pseudonymous identifier (e.g. REVIEWER-001). No unnecessary personal information is required; identity handling may occur outside the repository, but the identifier must be stable across this reviewer's submissions.

reviewer.description: intake alias: must equal reviewer_id (checked by VERIFY_SUBMISSION.py)

declaration.description: the reviewer's own statement that they had no role in producing the artifact and no interest in its approval

relationship_to_project.description: any relationship worth disclosing; 'none' is a fine answer

is_release_decision_authority.description: whether this reviewer is also the release decision authority. true requires policy_exception naming the recorded policy that explicitly permits the overlap; no such policy currently exists.

policy_exception.description: the recorded policy permitting reviewer/decision-authority overlap, or null

independence.description: The declaration is verified to exist mechanically; whether it is credible is a human judgment recorded in triage, never manufactured by automation.

artifact_digest.description: the digest of the artifact this review binds to; must be one of the five digests in ARTIFACT_IDENTITY.json

independently_computed_digest.description: the digest the reviewer computed themselves from the bytes they reviewed; must be one of the five subject digests. The repository's claim about identity is not to be trusted — this field is the reviewer's own measurement.

digest_basis.description: which artifact form independently_computed_digest was computed over (recommended)

digest_computation.description: how the digest was computed (command or method), so the measurement is reproducible (recommended)

review_scope_version.description: the frozen scope version this review answers (REVIEW_SCOPE.md)

scope.description: intake field: free-text scope statement; state the artifact and the scope version

date.description: intake alias: the record dates its own action; must equal review_end

scope_answers.description: recommended: an answer per frozen question, keyed SQ-1..SQ-8

findings.description: the reviewer's findings. May be empty — but the register closes nothing without per-finding evidence, so an empty list leaves every baseline finding undispositioned. Reviewers use their own finding identifiers; the project maintains the mapping and never requires its internal IDs.

reviewer_finding_id.description: the reviewer's own identifier for this finding, unique within the submission

affected_component.description: package, binary, service, or surface affected

applicability.description: whether the issue applies to the subject artifact as shipped. NOT_APPLICABLE without supporting evidence is held at REQUIRES_FURTHER_ANALYSIS by the register — 'not exploitable' alone is not sufficient.

evidence.description: what establishes the conclusion: commands, attached logs (pin them in attachmentDigests), reachability analysis

recommended_disposition.description: the reviewer's recommendation. For confirmed Critical findings the project may accept only FIX_BEFORE_ALPHA, ACCEPTED_RISK (with a named authority, rationale, scope impact, and expiry) or NOT_APPLICABLE (with establishing evidence).

baseline_advisory.description: the public advisory identifier (GHSA-/CVE-) of the FINDINGS_BASELINE.json row this finding addresses, or null for a finding outside the baseline. This is the reconciliation hook; the project's internal SEC-BL-NNN identifiers are never required of the reviewer.

attachmentDigests.description: sha256 per attachment filename; the intake recomputes these from the ingested bytes and refuses a mismatch
